evidence.paraphrase: The narrating dog describes its instinctive friendly reaction to being spoken to by a man.
evidence.quote:
It may be weak of me, but a man has only to speak to me and a sort
      of thrill goes right down my spine and sets my tail wagging.

evidence.paraphrase: The dog narrator contrasts its own sociable nature with its mother's one-man-dog aloofness.
evidence.quote:
Now, I'm a mixer. I can't help it. It's my nature. I like men. I like the
      taste of their boots, the smell of their legs, and the sound of their
      voices.

evidence.paraphrase: The dog reasons through the repeated punishments and revises the lessons taught by its mother.
evidence.quote:
I thought it out till my head ached, and finally I got it right. I began
      to see that mother's outlook was narrow.

evidence.paraphrase: The dog describes testing a behavior, observing the negative result, and changing its approach through reasoning.
evidence.quote:
What I had to do was to forget the training I had had from mother,
      sound as it no doubt was as a general thing, and to adapt myself to the
      needs of the particular man who had happened to buy me. I had tried
      mother's way, and all it had brought me was walloping, so now I would
      think for myself.

evidence.paraphrase: The narrating dog contrasts pedigree prize dogs with itself, a mongrel, addressing the reader directly.
evidence.quote:
Any dog will tell you what these prize-ribbon dogs are like. Their heads are so
      swelled they have to go into their kennels backwards.

evidence.paraphrase: The dog reacts with apology upon realizing the animal it attacked was a toy-dog, not a rat.
evidence.quote:
I'm sure I beg your pardon, sir,' I said apologetically. 'I thought you
      were a rat.

evidence.paraphrase: Tied up and awaiting being shot, the dog reflects with resignation and sadness.
evidence.quote:
It was all over. It had been pleasant while it lasted, but I had reached
      the end of my tether now. I don't think I was frightened, but a sense of
      pathos stole over me.

evidence.paraphrase: The dog narrator contrasts the perverse outcomes of its efforts, drawing a general lesson about luck.
evidence.quote:
When I did everything I could to please people, they wanted to
      shoot me; and when I did nothing except run away, they brought me back and
      treated me better than the most valuable prize-winner in the kennels.
